newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH MINFIN MULLS SLOWER ZLOTY DEVALUATION.
newsitem.headline: POLISH MINFIN MULLS SLOWER ZLOTY DEVALUATION.

text.p: Poland is considering a slower pace of monthly zloty devaluation to help curb inflation, Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka told Reuters Financial Television in an interview on Thursday.

"If the monthly inflation rate is consistently now under one percent and industrial prices are rising at the rate of 0.4-0.6 percent a month then a monthly devalution of one percent is clearly pro-export and not anti-inflationary," he said.
"So we are starting to think about the decelerating of the crawl. When? I'm not going to tell you," Belka said.
The zloty is now devalued by one percent a month against a basket of five western currencies to compensate for the still high inflation, at 14.6 percent in year-on-year terms in May.
The crawling devaluation, the rate of which is set by the independent central bank, was last cut on January 8, 1996, by 0.2 point.
